column1: # TUNING corpus: hand-picked real-world files from GitHub that rules have been designed against. Numbers measured
# on these files overstate accuracy; `github-holdout.tsv` is the measure of generalization.
# The files belong to their repositories and stay under those repositories' licenses. They are not copied into this
# repository or the published package: `scripts/fetch-github-corpus.mjs` downloads them to a local directory, and the
# evidence harnesses only read them to compute aggregate numbers. Each file is pinned to a commit.
# Batch 1 (126 files, 11 languages): the corpus the detector was tuned on as a prototype.
#   Hand-picked real-world corpus from GitHub: source files that carry business logic in popular, unarchived
#   repositories. Excluded: tests, examples, demos, documentation, third-party code vendored into a repository
#   (such as the Bootstrap 2 copy inside publify), malware source collections (vxunderground/MalwareSourceCode),
#   iTerm2 was on the list originally, but its sources/ moved into deeply nested subdirectories; FLEX, another
# Batch 2 (504 files, 12 per language for all 42 languages, permissively licensed repositories): selected as a
# holdout without running the detector, then used to find and fix cross-family misdetections, so it is tuning data
